subject.title: Standardize async resource lifecycle management across retry/cleanup paths

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared async resource lifecycle primitive across embedded retry cleanup, plugin/channel cleanup, and gateway/session shutdown, and where should that API live?
rationale: Current main has targeted fixes but no shared primitive; choosing a cross-boundary lifecycle contract could affect core architecture and plugin SDK compatibility, which automation should not decide.

options.title: Design a narrow shared contract
options.body: Keep this open and define the smallest owner boundary, API shape, migration path, and proof matrix before implementation.

options.title: Continue targeted fixes only
options.body: Close or narrow this tracker if maintainers decide per-surface guards are the desired architecture for now.

options.title: Limit to plugin/channel SDK
options.body: Route only the plugin resource-cleanup part into a backward-compatible plugin SDK lifecycle seam and leave embedded retry/session cleanup local.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow shared contract
recommendation.body: Keep this open and define the smallest owner boundary, API shape, migration path, and proof matrix before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to recent adjacent work on session lifecycle, plugin/channel lifecycle helpers, and embedded cleanup, making this the strongest routing signal for the design decision.
